name: HighLevel
subcategory: all-in-one agency and business operating system
tagline: Run lead capture, marketing, communications, sales, and customer operations in one platform

pricing.notes: Official Starter monthly price. The plan includes three sub-accounts.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (14-day trial; billing starts automatically unless canceled)
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (10 months' price for 12 months); no long-term contract
pricing.hiddenCosts: Phone numbers, SMS, email and premium AI are usage-billed even during trial. Optional add-ons include AI Employee $50 or $97/sub-account/mo, branded portal $49/sub-account/mo, dedicated IP $59/IP/mo, HIPAA $297/mo, listings $30/sub-account/mo, prospecting $29/sub-account/mo, premium support $500/mo, SEO $79/sub-account/mo, WhatsApp $10/sub-account/mo, white-label mobile app $497/mo and WordPress hosting from $10/site/mo.

verdictSummary: HighLevel is not a basic CRM. It is a broad operating system for agencies and businesses, bringing hundreds of features under one roof: lead capture, funnels, CRM, marketing, communications, booking, payments, websites, automation, AI, client sub-accounts, and SaaS resale. A constrained local lead-management starter is buildable, but a faithful replacement is not a one-shot project.
coreLoopDIY: Build one narrow local slice for one business: capture inquiries, manage contacts and deals, schedule follow-ups, and send a few consented email messages.
whatYouLose: the wider operating system: funnels, websites, reputation, memberships, and client portals
agency sub-accounts, white-label SaaS resale, and centralized administration
managed phone, SMS, and email delivery infrastructure
calendar, payments, AI, reporting, mobile apps, and third-party integrations
support, uptime, and compliance operations across the stack
moatNotes: The CRM is only one surface. The product's value is the growing connected operating system and the agency infrastructure that keeps its many parts working together.
whyPeopleStillPay: Agencies pay because HighLevel consolidates an expanding set of customer-acquisition and customer-operations tools into one configured system. Each client workspace accumulates connected phones, email domains, calendars, payments, pages, automations, data, and habits. The subscription buys maintained integrations, deliverability and telephony operations, multi-account administration, and a single support boundary when a flow fails.

prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow local lead-management starter inspired by one slice of HighLevel, in an empty repository.
Do not portray it as a HighLevel replacement.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture inquiries, manage contacts and deals, schedule follow-ups, and send a few consented email messages for one business.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all data locally by default and provide CSV import and export.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, deals, notes, tasks, configurable pipeline stages, and a next-action dashboard.
Add a public lead form with spam protection, consent capture, validation, and a clear success state.
Add saved filters, search, duplicate detection, merge, and a chronological interaction timeline.
Implement email templates and manual campaign sends through one token-based provider, with unsubscribe, suppression, rate limits, retries, and send logs.
Add role-based access for a tiny team, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Write focused tests for the core data flow and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, backup steps, and sending-domain setup.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out the operating-system breadth: agency sub-accounts, white-label resale, funnels, websites, memberships, phone and SMS provisioning, payment processing, OAuth integrations, workflow automation, AI, mobile apps, and enterprise reporting.
Do not claim to reproduce managed deliverability, telephony reliability, compliance operations, or a connector ecosystem.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
